title: AI sucks at making quality backend solutions for games. (informational repost)
author: Glittering_Focus1538
selftext:
So I made BoneScript, a Deterministic backend code generation compiler that completely reimagines how people and AI do backend development.  
  
BoneScript helps hobbyist game devs by letting you describe your game's backend in simple, high-level terms (like "players have inventory items with states, and a 'craft' action that checks resources then updates them"), then instantly generates a complete, runnable Node.js server with database, API endpoints, real-time WebSockets, auth, admin panel, and even Nakama support for multiplayer.

Instead of wiring up Express routes, SQL migrations, state machines, validation, events, and error handling manually, you focus on the game logic bones, constraints like "health > 0", state transitions like "alive → dead", or real-time channels for lobbies and the tool fills in the full professional skeleton deterministically every time.

For a hobbyist or vibecoder, this means prototyping a full player progression system or item trading backend in minutes, testing it locally with the generated admin UI and TypeScript client, then iterating by tweaking the description and recompiling, without getting buried in boilerplate or backend complexity.

replies.author: Glittering_Focus1538
replies.body:
Got Colyseus working end to end pretty easily. New stuff:

You can now build live multiplayer games. Write what a player looks like (score, position, whatever), declare a "room" type, and add actions like "move" or "attack" — the compiler builds the whole multiplayer server: lobbies, login checks so randoms can't spoof your account, real-time syncing so everyone sees the same game state, rules that block cheaters trying to send bogus moves, and auto-saving so a server crash doesn't lose progress. Pretty much the multiplayer skeleton you'd build for a co-op game, raid lobby, or chat room, generated for you.

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body: This is very interesting. How would you handle player movement with collisions with this system? Either unit to unit collision or terrain collisions?

replies.author: Glittering_Focus1538
replies.body: Speed capping works today via preconditions (server rejects moves exceeding max\_speed). Collision detection and physics are outside scope, BoneScript handles networking, state sync, and auth, not spatial logic. You'd use an `extension_point` or Colyseus's `setSimulationInterval` to plug in your own collision code, and BoneScript preserves it across recompilation.
